related_resources.reason: University of Cambridge editorial chronology of life and letters, 1809-1882.
Edited chronological chapters drawing on letters; history of family, publications and scientific network.
Dated route with landfalls and geological observations. Use area-centroid map proxies only.
Letters and historical introduction by Janet Browne covering the 1831-1836 voyage.
Henslow, FitzRoy, Beagle voyage, the marriage, Kent work and archive provenance.
Gould, Owen, 1837 transmutation notebooks, 1838 Malthus, 1842 outline and differences between observations and mechanism.
Darwin personally dates his 1837 notebook, 1842 sketch, 1844 essay and 1859 publication.
Distinguishes 1835 island observations and later Gould identification from the retrospective finch-epiphany myth.
History of unpublished 1842/1844 sketches, 1854 note sorting, and larger 1856-1858 manuscript.
1858 Wallace interruption, Lyell and Hooker, the 1859 book, and the family context.
The original published argument. Do not import twentieth-century Mendelian population genetics into its claims.
Wallace independent natural selection and the joint paper read to the Linnean Society in 1858.
Travel, biogeography, independent discovery, later relations and beliefs of Wallace.
Marriage, Down House, children, faith, family scientific work and household role.
Annie 1851 death and Darwin memorial; do not infer a single causal religious conversion.
Scholarly historical argument against the claim that Annie death caused Darwin to lose Christianity.
Religion, deathbed-conversion myth, and Darwin reticence on personal beliefs.
Evidence from symptom letters, health diary and changing working routine. No retrospective definitive diagnosis.
1846-1854 barnacle studies and four monographs, and their relation to taxonomy and scientific reputation.
The Chonos specimen, Hooker advice and how the barnacle program started.
Darwin original account of gradual subsidence, reef types and geological inference.
Seed salt-water experiments motivated by plant distribution and long-distance dispersal.
Reported quantitative results and openly corrected his assumption about floating plants.
Breeders, pigeons and the use of artificial selection as explanatory analogy.
Botanical experiments, garden and greenhouse, Kent family working base.
Madagascan orchid and proposed long-tongued insect pollinator; later corroboration.
Context and documentary uncertainty around the 1860 Wilberforce-Huxley discussion.
Birthplace, education, death, Beagle, professional and family data.
Funeral and burial 26 April 1882; place of death is Kent, burial is a posthumous event.

spacetime_coverage.subject: Charles Robert Darwin
spacetime_coverage.description: Documented birthplace, education, approximate Beagle landfalls and field-work regions, and later scientific bases. Shipboard travel is represented as dated stops or coarse region points, not continuous geographic occupancy. Modern countries group places rather than assert their nineteenth-century borders. Wallace correspondence and posthumous burial are not mapped as Darwin research travel.
